payload.title: Event-driven GitHub integrations for Kanbus
payload.description:
## Purpose
Make GitHub events a dependable trigger for keeping Kanbus cloud data current and, later, for reacting to pull-request, review, and CI lifecycle changes.

## Why this exists
The single-worker Issue Router can dispatch from Kanbus issue state without GitHub webhooks. Webhooks are a complementary integration surface for changes originating in GitHub, not a prerequisite for task dispatch and not a replacement queue.

## Direction
- Start with signed GitHub push events that trigger an idempotent tenant-repository sync and publish a Kanbus-visible change signal.
- Preserve Git as the durable source of truth; treat webhook deliveries and SQS messages as triggers that request reconciliation.
- Tolerate duplicate, delayed, and reordered delivery through verification, deduplication, retries, and a dead-letter path.
- Enforce tenant isolation and least-privilege access to webhook secrets and cloud resources.
- Add PR, review, and CI triggers only as separate, explicit follow-up slices when a concrete router or board behavior needs them.

## Success
A reproducible signed webhook test causes the correct tenant repository to reconcile and the resulting change to become visible through Kanbus, with observable retry/failure behavior and no cross-tenant access.

## Out of scope
This initiative is not required for the first single-worker dispatch milestone, does not make GitHub the Kanbus issue source of truth, and does not authorize automatic pull-request merging.
